content: Medroxyprogesterone is a type of hormone classified as a progestin. It mimics the natural progesterone produced by the body and is prescribed to replace this hormone when the body does not produce sufficient amounts. This medication has multiple uses, including the treatment of amenorrhea (absence of menstrual periods) and abnormal uterine bleeding. It is also used as part of combination hormone replacement therapy (HRT) with estrogens to alleviate menopausal symptoms such as hot flashes. Before starting this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Take the medication orally as directed by your doctor, adhering strictly to the prescribed dosing schedule. If you have any questions, consult your doctor. For the treatment of amenorrhea or abnormal uterine bleeding, the medication is typically taken once daily for 5 to 10 days during the second half of the planned menstrual cycle or as directed by your physician. Common side effects may include nausea, bloating, breast tenderness, headache, changes in vaginal discharge, mood swings, blurred vision, dizziness, drowsiness, or weight changes (gain or loss). Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. However, in rare cases, especially when used in combination with estrogen products, it may cause serious and potentially fatal complications such as blood clots (e.g., heart attack, stroke, clots in the lungs, legs, or eyes). Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you experience any side effects, contact your doctor for medical advice. In the United States, you can also call 1-800-222-1222 for poison control assistance. In Canada, call 1-844-764-7669. Before taking medroxyprogesterone, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. Some Canadian brands of this product may contain inactive ingredients, such as soybean, which can trigger allergic reactions or other issues. Individuals allergic to peanuts may also be allergic to soy. This medication may cause dizziness or drowsiness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This medication may cause melasma, which appears as blotchy, dark areas on the face and skin. Sunlight can worsen this condition, so limit your time in the sun and avoid tanning booths and sunlamps. Use sunscreen and wear protective clothing when outdoors. This medication should not be used during pregnancy, as it may harm the fetus. Additionally, medroxyprogesterone passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain medications, such as rifamycins (e.g., rifampin), may affect the removal of medroxyprogesterone from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. This medication may also interfere with certain laboratory tests, leading to false results. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. While taking this medication, regular physical exams, including laboratory and medical tests (e.g., blood pressure checks, breast exams/mammograms, pelvic exams, Pap smears), should be conducted as directed by your doctor. Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examining your breasts and report any lumps immediately. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Medroxyprogesterone is sometimes used in combination with estrogen as part of hormone replacement therapy (HRT) in postmenopausal women. However, combination HRT can rarely cause serious side effects, including heart disease (e.g., heart attacks), stroke, blood clots (e.g., in the lungs and legs), dementia, and breast cancer. The risks may depend on the duration of treatment and other factors. Combination HRT should be used for the shortest possible duration at the lowest effective dose to minimize the risk of serious side effects. It should not be used to prevent heart disease or dementia. Discuss the risks and benefits of treatment with your doctor, considering your personal health history. If you use this medication for an extended period, you should undergo a complete physical exam at regular intervals (e.g., annually) or as directed by your doctor. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
